sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168][F1][F10].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 jump came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices across all products, and the three years to FY2025 show a 5.3% annual decline [F8][D274][P47][D844].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth, while non-U.S. added 2.0pp [D382][D384][D342][D400].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but grew only 0.1%, contributing 0.1pp, while natural gas grew 37.4% and contributed 4.4pp [D551][D552][D553][D585][D586].
FY2025 sales rose on higher volumes of $6,197 million, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 against 4.9% revenue growth, so there was no operating leverage [D343][D342].
Basic EPS fell 18.7%, faster than net income, because the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D344][D343][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Cost of revenue rose to 37.9% of revenue from 36.6%, and D&A to 19.5% from 17.5%, a 1.3pp and 2.0pp drag [D326][D292][D330][D296].
DD&A increased $1,901 million in FY2025, primarily from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell $265 million, mainly the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.07x window median [F59][F20][D333][D855].
The FY2025 decline from $20.1 billion came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue, and capex of $12.6 billion absorbed most of it [D331][P7].
D&A was 19.5% of revenue in FY2025, up from 17.5% in FY2024 [D330][D296].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025, up 13.4%, against $1.0 billion of current debt [D335][D357][X203].
Net cash cannot be ranked: long-term debt is missing after FY2020, so the pack omits net debt for FY2025 [R6].
FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capex, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the 30% framework [D339][P31].
Revenue in the table is a later recast: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion first reported, so growth and margins mix two presentations [R1][F10][X10].
Long-term debt is absent after FY2020, so net debt and its peer rank cannot be computed for FY2025 [R6][F157].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized commodity prices, the one clear demand-side break in the window [R2][F8][D274][P47].
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of consolidated FY2025 revenue, so segment shares must not be added [R4].
Net margin: a print below the 17.9% window median would confirm the FY2022-to-FY2025 slide; a recovery above it would reverse it [D831][F30].
Operating cash flow: a fall below the FY2025 $19.8 billion would extend the FY2024-FY2025 decline, reported in the next 10-K [F59][D346].
Diluted share count: a further rise above the FY2025 1,253.4 million shares would keep EPS falling faster than net income [X131][D356].
